prompts.orchestratorRoadmap:
ROADMAP-DRIVEN PLANNING
Read {roadmapFile} before deciding anything. It is the authoritative plan; {taskFile} is only ever ONE small step out of it.

EXECUTION ORDER — work these units strictly in this order, finishing each before starting the next:
  1. Section 3 'Remaining Legacy Work Inventory', P1 'Important Production Work' — the Windows signal-timing test guards, and socket disconnection state re-attachment. Note that every P0 item is annotated '(Addressed in Phase 7)', so do NOT dispatch P0 separately; it is delivered by Phase 7 and dispatching it twice would duplicate work. P2 is deferred post-Phase-10 or declared OBSOLETE: no tasks.
  2. Phase 7 (Section 5), which delivers Initiative A — release channels, the versioned migration engine, runtime isolation — and closes the P0 blockers above.
  3. Phase 8 (Section 5), which delivers Initiative B — shared team agents and multi-user governance.
  4. Phase 9, then Phase 10, as specified in Section 5.
Sections 4's Initiative A and B are the architectural specifications for Phases 7 and 8; read them as the design detail for those phases, not as separate units of work.

Break the current unit into PR-sized tasks: one coherent change a reviewer could read in a sitting, independently verifiable, leaving the tree in a working state. A unit is normally several such tasks. Dispatch exactly ONE of them — the next one — per turn.
Decide per task whether it needs verification: write {testSpecFile} when the tester must run something, and omit it when the change genuinely cannot be tested (docs, config), saying so in the task itself.

UNIT BOUNDARIES — when the current unit looks finished, do NOT move on yet. First verify it:
  - re-read that unit's goals and acceptance criteria in {roadmapFile};
  - check the completed reports and the git history actually satisfy every one of them;
  - confirm nothing was silently dropped, stubbed, or deferred along the way, and that any DEC register entries it cites are honoured.
If anything is missing, the next task is to finish it — the unit is not done. Only when it is genuinely complete, write "Status: PHASE_COMPLETE" to {taskFile} with a short summary of what the unit delivered and how you verified it, so the human can review the boundary.
After the human resumes you will be asked to plan again. If {taskFile} still holds a "PHASE_COMPLETE" marker at that point, it has already been reviewed and approved — do NOT restate it. Read {roadmapFile} afresh, pick up the next unit in the order above, and replace {taskFile} with the first task of that unit.
